name: Ben-deker
overview: Ben-deker was a male figure who served as one of King Solomon's twelve deputies, a position of administrative authority in the kingdom. He was specifically assigned to oversee the district of Makaz, indicating a trusted role in Solomon's government. No additional tribal affiliation or personal notes are recorded about him in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Ben-deker means 'son of Deker' with the root idea of 'pierces.' This proper name is noted in 1 Kings 4:9 but is not described as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Ben-deker beyond his role as one of Solomon's deputies. There are no known relatives or descendants mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ben-deker's significance lies in his administrative role under King Solomon, reflecting the organized and delegated governance during Solomon's reign. As one of the twelve deputies, he contributed to the effective management of the kingdom's resources and regions, exemplifying the wisdom and order Solomon's administration sought to maintain. His mention in 1 Kings highlights the practical aspects of Solomon's rule rather than personal or prophetic narratives.
